pages.class_justification: The constructed OWF is $G$ itself, so the construction uses the hypothesis PRG only as an oracle; the security reduction runs any inverter once as an oracle and outputs $1$ iff the returned $\hat{x}$ satisfies $G(\hat{x}) = y$. This is the RTV04 fully-black-box shape.
pages.statement: Any [[pseudorandom-generator|PRG]] $G : \bits^n \to \bits^m$ with $m > n$ is a [[hash-function#preimage-resistance-one-wayness|one-way function]]: an inverter for $G$ with success probability $\varepsilon$ yields a PRG distinguisher with advantage at least $\varepsilon - 2^{n-m}$, since a uniform $y \in \bits^m$ has a $G$-preimage with probability at most $2^{n-m}$ — folklore. The conclusion is one-wayness only, not collision resistance.
pages.sketch: The OWF is $G$ itself. Given an inverter $\calA$, the distinguisher $D(y)$ runs $\hat{x} \gets \calA(y)$ and outputs $1$ iff $G(\hat{x}) = y$: on $y = G(s)$ this happens with $\calA$'s success probability, on uniform $y$ with probability at most $2^{n-m}$.
flags: Conclusion 'hash-function' is the wiki's combined hash/OWF page (alias OWF); the edge is PRG => OWF and the statement pins the preimage-resistance variant via the page's declared anchor #preimage-resistance-one-wayness. The wiki's hash syntax is keyed ($\hash : \calK \times \calD \to \calR$); the PRG-as-OWF has a trivial key space.

The no-black-box-CRHF-from-OWP separation (Simon, EUROCRYPT 1998; cryptobib EC:Simon98, doi 10.1007/BFb0054137) is a barrier, not part of this edge; the statement only scopes the conclusion to one-wayness and asserts nothing about collision resistance.

The migrated quote's trailing 'so OWF <=> PRG' is a derived equivalence; the converse direction is [[hash-function-to-prg-hill99]] (HILL99). Both directions exist as separate pages, so kind stays implication.
The length-expansion hypothesis ($m > n$) is load-bearing and is definitional for the wiki's PRG page ($|\calR| > |\calS|$); the statement carries it explicitly.
verifier_changes: statement: quantified the distinguishing advantage ($\varepsilon - 2^{n-m}$) instead of 'yields a distinguisher'; replaced the uncited barrier claim 'a PRG does not generically yield collision resistance' with a scoping sentence that asserts nothing
sketch: tightened wording

sources.ref_file_title: GGM86 - How to construct random functions
sources.authors: Oded Goldreich, Shafi Goldwasser, Silvio Micali
sources.note: Verified against vendor/cryptobib entry GolGolMic86 (JACM 33(4):792-807, 1986, doi 10.1145/6490.6503) and the existing wiki reference page (cryptobib_key GolGolMic86).

pages.class_justification: The construction invokes the length-doubling PRG only as an oracle (one call per input bit); the security proof is a hybrid argument over the tree levels whose reduction runs any PRF distinguisher as an oracle to build a PRG distinguisher. This is the RTV04 fully-black-box shape, and the wiki's black-box-separations page uses this construction as its worked example of the notion.
pages.statement: A length-doubling [[pseudorandom-generator|PRG]] $G : \bits^n \to \bits^{2n}$ yields a [[pseudorandom-function|PRF]] with key space and range $\bits^n$ and domain $\bits^\ell$: $\KeyGen(1^\secpar)$ outputs $k \getsr \bits^n$ and, writing $G(s) = G_0(s) \| G_1(s)$, $\Eval(k, x_1 \cdots x_\ell) := G_{x_\ell}(G_{x_{\ell-1}}(\cdots G_{x_1}(k) \cdots))$ — [[GGM86 - How to construct random functions|GGM86]].
pages.sketch: The construction walks a binary tree of depth $\ell$: start from $k$ and, on bit $x_i$, keep the left or right half of $G$'s output. A hybrid over the $\ell$ tree levels reduces any $q$-query PRF distinguisher to a PRG distinguisher with a factor $q\ell$ loss.
flags: The factor-$q\ell$ loss in the sketch is the standard textbook hybrid analysis (levels times PRG instances per level, e.g. Boneh–Shoup's GGM theorem), not a concrete bound stated in GGM86 itself, which is asymptotic; security_loss left empty for that reason.

Pseudocode checked line by line against the PRF page's Syntax ($\Eval(k,x)$, key in $\calK$, deterministic) and the CLAUDE.md command table (\State, \Comment, \For/\EndFor, \Return); \algname{Algorithm} is not grouped by the pseudocode plugin (only Game/Oracle are), so it renders as a standalone block.
verifier_changes: statement: added the $\KeyGen$ line so the built PRF matches the PRF page's (\KeyGen, \Eval) syntax
sketch: minor tightening
flags: removed the unverifiable theorem number 'Thm 4.11'; recorded the pseudocode check

pages.class_justification: Composition of two fully-black-box links: the GGM construction calls the PRG only as an oracle, and the PRF-based randomized encryption calls the PRF only as an oracle; each security reduction runs its adversary only as an oracle (the CPA reduction answers encryption queries with its own PRF-oracle calls). Fully-black-box reductions compose, so the composed pair retains the RTV04 shape.
pages.statement: A length-doubling [[pseudorandom-generator|PRG]] implies CPA-secure [[symmetric-key-encryption|SKE]]: the PRG yields a [[pseudorandom-function|PRF]] ([[prg-to-prf-ggm86|PRG ⇒ PRF (GGM)]]), and $\Enc(k, m) = (r, \Eval(k, r) \oplus m)$ with fresh $r \getsr \calD$ is CPA-secure ([[prf-to-ske|PRF ⇒ CPA-secure SKE]]) — folklore. The fixed-pad stream cipher $\Enc(k, m) = G(k) \oplus m$ is deterministic, hence not CPA-secure; it is only one-time secure.
flags: CONFIRMED ERROR in the migrated statement (not in the edge): $\Enc(k,m) = G(k) \oplus m$ reuses one pad for every message, so two left-right oracle queries break CPA security under the SKE page's game; the scheme is only one-time secure. The edge PRG => CPA-SKE is true via the PRF route. The parent page content/Primitives/pseudorandom-generator.md still carries the wrong bullet and is already flagged in .fact-check/queue.json — fix it in the same commit that applies this page.

Composite-chain page: both links exist as prg-to-prf-ggm86 and prf-to-ske, so per schema/README this edge is derivable; consider deleting it or rescoping to 'PRG => one-time-secure SKE' (direct stream cipher). Rescoping is blocked today because the SKE page defines no one-time/EAV security notion.
The PRF-to-SKE link as written needs the PRF range to equal the message space (or CTR mode over blocks); prf-to-ske's own migrated sketch is separately flagged as deterministic/wrong.
verifier_changes: statement: added the load-bearing 'length-doubling' hypothesis that the GGM link needs; made the randomness domain explicit ($r \getsr \calD$); tightened the correction sentence
class_justification: named how the CPA reduction treats the adversary (oracle only) instead of asserting it

pages.class_justification: The iPRF is the PRP itself with $\Invert$ wrapped to return the singleton preimage set; both algorithms call the PRP only as oracles. The security reduction runs any distinguisher unchanged as a PRP distinguisher; the remaining ideal-world gap (random permutation vs. random function, forward queries only) is the information-theoretic switching-lemma term and needs no access to the adversary's code.
pages.statement: A [[pseudorandom-permutation|PRP]] over a domain $\calD$ with $|\calD|$ superpolynomial in $\secpar$ is an [[pseudorandom-function#invertible-prfs|invertible PRF]] under the traditional (forward-oracle) game $\Game^{\mathrm{prf}}$: the iPRF's inversion algorithm returns the singleton $\{\Invert(k, y)\}$, and for every $q$-query $\calA$ the PRF advantage is at most the PRP advantage plus the [[switching-lemma|Switching Lemma]] term $O(q^2/|\calD|)$, as in [[prp-to-prf|PRP ⇒ PRF]] — folklore. Strong security under $\Game^{\mathrm{iprf}}$, where $\calA$ also queries the inversion oracle, fails for every permutation: $\Invert(k, y)$ is never empty, while a random function's preimage set is empty with constant probability.
pages.sketch: A permutation is an iPRF with singleton preimage sets and perfect correctness. For forward queries only, a random permutation is statistically within $O(q^2/|\calD|)$ of a random function, so PRP security transfers to the traditional PRF game with birthday loss.
pages.security_loss: $O(q^2/|\calD|)$ for $q$ queries, per the switching lemma
notes_to_keep: The strong game $\Game^{\mathrm{iprf}}$ gives $\calA$ an inversion oracle, so the forward-only switching lemma does not reach it; the statement is scoped to the traditional game. Flagged against both parent pages in the fact-check queue.
flags: Verifier re-derived the strong-iPRF failure: under $\Game^{\mathrm{iprf}}$ as defined on pseudorandom-function.md the ideal world is a random function $\calD \to \calR$ with a preimage-SET oracle. A single inversion query on a fresh $y$ returns a singleton for any permutation but the empty set with probability $(1-1/|\calD|)^{|\calD|} \approx 1/e$ for a random function on $\calD \to \calD$ — a one-query distinguisher with constant advantage. The fact-check queue's suggestion that 'sPRP plus a two-sided switching lemma' would suffice is therefore wrong for this game (a two-sided switching lemma compares against a random permutation with inverse oracle, not a random function with preimage-set oracle). The statement now records the failure with its one-line reason.

HPPY25 (Plinko), which introduced the iPRF notion cited on prf-to-invertible-prf-hppy25, does not state this PRP observation in its abstract; the claim is left folklore with the switching lemma as the technique (kept in via:).
Provenance is consistent with prp-to-prf, now sourced to IR89 for the switching argument; this page is its trivial corollary and links to it rather than re-citing.

notes_to_keep: shortened to one line
class_justification: minor tightening

sources.ref_file_title: IR89 - Limits on the provable consequences of one-way permutations
sources.note: Existing wiki reference page (content/References/IR89 - ...; its cryptobib_key is C:ImpRud88, the CRYPTO 1988 version; cryptobib also has STOC:ImpRud89, doi 10.1145/73007.73012). The PRP/PRF switching lemma — a $q$-query distinguisher separates a random permutation from a random function with probability $O(q^2/2^n)$ — is used there to replace the random-permutation oracle by a random-function oracle. Attribution confirmed by verifier only via WebSearch snippets of secondary sources: Chang–Nandi eprint 2008/078, Affeldt et al. ProvSec 2007 ('the standard proof of the PRP/PRF Switching Lemma is due to Impagliazzo and Rudich'), and eprint 2023/1083 ('originally due to Impagliazzo and Rudich in 1989'); IR89's text itself was egress-blocked.

sources.ref_file_title: BR06 - The Security of Triple Encryption and a Framework for Code-Based Game-Playing Proofs
sources.note: Verified against vendor/cryptobib entry EC:BelRog06 (EUROCRYPT 2006, pp. 409-426, doi 10.1007/11761679_25 — suggested cryptobib_key: EC:BelRog06). Full version eprint 2004/331 under the title 'Code-Based Game-Playing Proofs and the Security of Triple Encryption' (confirmed via WebSearch snippet). Names the PRP/PRF Switching Lemma, exhibits the conditioning flaw in the standard proof (observed by Kohno), and gives the game-playing proof with bound $q(q-1)/2^{n+1}$.

sources.ref_file_title: Din20 - On the Streaming Indistinguishability of a Random Permutation and a Random Function
sources.note: Existing wiki reference page (cryptobib_key EC:Dinur20b); already cited on the switching-lemma page for the memory-bounded improvement.

pages.class_justification: The construction is the identity: the PRP's $\Eval$ is used unchanged as the PRF, so the hypothesis is invoked only as an oracle. The security reduction runs any PRF distinguisher once, unchanged, as a PRP distinguisher; the remaining ideal-world gap (random permutation vs. random function) is the information-theoretic switching-lemma term and needs no access to the adversary's code.
pages.statement: A [[pseudorandom-permutation|PRP]] over a domain $\calD$ with $|\calD|$ superpolynomial in $\secpar$ is a [[pseudorandom-function|PRF]] with $\Eval$ unchanged: for every $q$-query $\calA$, $\Adv^{\mathrm{prf}}_{\PRP,\calA}(\secpar) \le \Adv^{\mathrm{prp}}_{\PRP,\calA}(\secpar) + O(q^2/|\calD|)$ by the [[switching-lemma|Switching Lemma]], and the additive term is negligible for superpolynomial $|\calD|$ — [[IR89 - Limits on the provable consequences of one-way permutations|IR89]].
pages.sketch: In the ideal worlds, a random permutation and a random function on $\calD$ are statistically indistinguishable up to the birthday bound $O(q^2/|\calD|)$ — an output collision is the only distinguishing event — so any PRF distinguisher is a PRP distinguisher with an additive $O(q^2/|\calD|)$ loss.

pages.statement: $\classQCMA \subseteq \classQMA$: the QMA verifier measures the witness register in the computational basis and runs the QCMA verifier on the outcome. Completeness holds with the classical witness sent as a basis state; soundness holds because measuring any quantum witness yields a distribution over classical strings, and the acceptance probability is the average of the QCMA acceptance probabilities over it — folklore.
